newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-NO EXTRA MEASURES ON MONEY MARKET NEEDED-C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-NO EXTRA MEASURES ON MONEY MARKET NEEDED-C.BANK.

text.p: The Estonian central bank said on Monday that it has no intention to apply any additional measures to avoid instability and illiquidity in the interbank overnight market.
"The central bank thinks no additional measures are needed although it will keep a constant eye on backing the fluent operation of the system," a central bank spokesperson told Reuters.

The average interest rates in Estonia's money market rose to over six percent last week in two days. The one-week overnight average interest lending rate TALIBOR rose by 0.93 basis points on Wednesday to 5.43 percent.
The spokesperson said that while liquidity was lower than usual, the fluctuation remained within the usual monthly levels.
The central bank does not support the commercial banks' idea of informing money market participants of the market situation during the day, the spokesperson added.
